# Thothica

> AI systems for institutions that run on records. Thothica writes the ontology, deploys the agents that fill it, builds the system staff work in, and runs it in production. Four layers, one company, so the layers agree with each other.

Thothica (legal name: Thothica Private Limited) is an AI startup based in New Delhi, India, founded in 2023. Its discipline is data ontology. Contact: hello@thothica.com. This file describes the site, its case studies and its use cases so that LLMs and crawlers can understand them without rendering the pages.

## The stack

Thothica is not a software vendor. It delivers four layers, all of them in-house, which is normally four suppliers and a systems integrator.

- **L1, Ontology. We write down what your data means.** Our software reads the systems you already run and writes the first draft: what each record is, how it links to the others, and who has to sign off. We set the rules it follows and check what it produces. Reads from SAP, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, SharePoint, Excel, Tally, MS Access, CSV exports, scanned PDFs, legacy portals and paper registers.
- **L2, Agents and engineers. We sit with your experts, in software or in person.** Much of what decides an outcome was never written down anywhere; it is in the head of the officer who has done the job for eleven years. The job is the same either way: ask how the work is actually done and write the answers into the same structure as everything else. Thothica does this in two modes, chosen by the situation rather than sold as a package. Forward deployed agents are software that works through the systems staff already use, and are sent when the knowledge is spread thinly across many people and the work can be done through existing systems. Forward deployed engineers are Thothica's own people working in the client's building, and are sent when the problem is new, when nothing may leave the premises, or when two departments have to settle a definition before anything can be written down.
- **L3, Application. We build the system your staff work in.** Either we build it, or we put the layer inside the software you already use. Either way an answer arrives as something a person can act on, with the record it came from attached to it.
- **L4, Operation. We run it, and we keep running it.** Five government portals, a hundred-year-old archive, a publishing line and a newsroom engine are live on this stack right now, and we operate them. We do not hand over the code and leave.

## What Thothica does

An ontology is the written answer to what an organization's data means: which column matters, why two departments use different words for one thing, who signs off. Today it sits in a few people's heads.

Thothica writes it down for whatever system a client already runs, in whatever field they work in.

Thothica's software reads a client's systems and writes the first version of the ontology. It works out what each item means, how the items relate to one another, and who decides. Thothica sets the rules it follows and checks its work. The client's staff and AI can then both ask it questions, and every answer shows which record it came from.

The organization no longer depends on only a few experienced people to interpret its data. It can solve, at scale, the problems those people used to solve one at a time.

## What an ontology is made of

An ontology has three parts. Together, these three are the ontology, written down in one place and one structure, so that people and software read the same thing.

- **Data sources, what you have.** Scanned PDFs, spreadsheets and CSV files, databases, legacy systems, SAP and other enterprise software. It does not matter where the data sits; Thothica's software writes the connection to each source, so nothing has to be moved or typed in again.
- **Logic sources, what you know.** Formulas buried in spreadsheets, existing code, machine learning models, written rules and prompts. Some of it is in no system at all: it sits with the people who have done the job for years. Thothica sends in forward deployed agents, software that works alongside a client's experts, asks them how the job is really done, and writes the answers down in the same structure as everything else.
- **Systems of action, what you do.** An ERP, existing portals, a new system Thothica builds, or an AI agent. Thothica builds the system the client acts in, or puts the layer inside the one they already use, so a decision arrives as a step someone can take.

## Case studies: five systems in production

Every case study is summarised on the home page at https://thothica.com/#case-studies, and each has its own page with diagrams, linked below.

- **Five Portals, One Read-Only AI Layer** (https://thothica.com/case-studies/government-portals/). Thothica built the AI layer that now runs on five state government portals, each built on a different technology and each storing its data differently. For each portal Thothica first wrote down what its data measures and every way it can legitimately be broken down (by district, by scheme, by month, by status), then classified the portal's free-text fields into a fixed set so they could be counted. On one portal that classification made 115,652 separate decisions about what a piece of text meant. An official asks a question in plain language and gets an answer taken from that portal's own records, with every figure traceable back to the rows it came from. The layer holds read permission only and cannot alter a record. Across all five the method did not change; the catalogue content did.
- **A Century of Writing, Searchable by Who Said What** (https://thothica.com/case-studies/think-tank-archive/). More than 1,000 primary works from an intellectual tradition going back to the 1850s, held as more than 2,000 PDFs that were mostly photographs of printed pages on a slow website. Thothica's software turned the pictures into text across five languages and several scripts, then built the ontology in four layers: works (document type, series, position in a run), people (506 writers resolved to one identity each across scripts, spellings and initials), relations (who wrote what, who is the subject of what, who is mentioned inside what, who argued with whom), and positions (where each writer sits in the tradition on several independent axes). Every relation carries the verbatim passage that proves it, checked as a substring of the source text; a relation whose quotation fails that check is discarded rather than kept with a warning, so a fabricated quotation cannot survive storage. Roughly three quarters of writers came out of the first classification pass flagged for human review. The archive is split into two declared tiers: clean text that software may quote directly with paragraph-level addresses, and scanned works that software must describe and link out to rather than quote.
- **Graphic Stories at Scale, Every Line Traced to a Source** (https://thothica.com/case-studies/graphic-stories/). For one of India's largest publishers, a research corpus of roughly ten million words (70+ books converted and chaptered, 220+ interviews transcribed) spanning several publishing lines (illustrated biographies, India's classical epics and traditional knowledge, health and social-awareness titles, an original early-reader universe, activity books), organized on one ontology: Line, Program, Subject, then Dossier as input and Book as output. Length and format are declared per title and enforced by the machine, rather than fixed across the catalogue. Sources are split chapter-per-file so a claim can point at an exact file and line, which is what makes the citation contract mechanically checkable rather than a promise somebody has to keep by hand. Because every subject's research sits in one corpus, the library already holds passages where other people describe this subject; finding them uses entity anchoring (the name, its likely mangled forms, and the person's companies, teams and signature events) with the speaker confirmed from content rather than from a speaker label, because transcripts garble names and mislabel speakers. Every beat in a finished script carries a pointer to its source line, and a gate resolves each pointer before the script proceeds. Characters, backgrounds and finished pages are generated by frontier image models against locked visual specifications per figure, and the output ships both as press-ready separated colour with single-ink black text and as editable pages in the book's own lettering, neither of which comes out of an image tool by default. The pipeline is deployed and running. Titles come off it continuously across five publishing lines, and each new line added extends the same machinery instead of needing its own.
- **A Newsroom That Runs Unattended and Publishes Nothing** (https://thothica.com/case-studies/cricket-content-engine/). An engine that reads live match data, the news wire and fan forums, plans its own slate, writes in the publisher's voice against a written style specification, corroborates its claims against sources it actually fetches, and then stops at a private editorial queue where a human decides what runs. Its taxonomy is a declared ontology in one manifest that every consumer reads from; each dimension states its kind, whether an item may carry one value or several, and what happens to an unfamiliar value: closed dimensions fail the build, curated dimensions warn, and auto-grow dimensions accept and queue for curation so coverage of a debut is never blocked. Aliases resolve every known form of a name to one identity so counts cannot fragment. The engine holds only a data-read key and push access to one repository; it holds no credential that can publish to the public site.
- **Handwritten Registers Turned Into Verified Rows** (https://thothica.com/case-studies/olympiad-forms/). Schools submit registrations on pre-printed grids and hand-ruled registers. The doctrine is that the model does perception and the code does arithmetic: a vision model transcribes what is on the paper, and every sum, reconciliation and verdict is computed deterministically afterwards. The independence rule follows: evidence that confirms a reading must come from a source independent of it, so a total read in the same pass may contradict the marks but may never confirm them. The handwritten total is read again separately and voted on, then pinned so a later repair cannot rewrite the number it is measured against. No checksum does not mean verified: a sheet with no usable checksum is reported as unverified, not as a match. Paper that contradicts itself is flagged, never silently repaired. The guarantee is not perfect accuracy. It is that nothing wrong is shipped without being flagged.

## Use cases: built to order, by institution

Organized by the kind of institution asking, and summarised on the home page at https://thothica.com/#use-cases. Each has its own page, linked below. These are capabilities rather than delivered engagements.

- **Collections That Answer Questions** (https://thothica.com/use-cases/archives/). Capture (scanning, fragile and bound material, oral-history recording), making pages and recordings readable, then the ontology over the collection, then publication to people as a platform and to machines as an open interface exposing defined operations (list works, fetch a record, get an exact passage, search, find related) with no language model inside it, so the researcher's own assistant does the reasoning and the institution's tier rules travel with the data. Also: citation intelligence (who cites the collection, which holdings earn use, whether citations are well formed, where the collection is invisible, and unattributed use found by matching text), physical media tracking (location, condition, carrier obsolescence, retention clocks, link to digital surrogates), and reissuing backlist material as web editions with stable addresses, reflowable e-books and fresh print-ready files from one structured source.
- **A Different Use Case per Department** (https://thothica.com/use-cases/government/). Not one use case. Industry and investment promotion (eligibility ontology behind a single window). Revenue and arrears (public registers normalised, deterministic rule-based detection with each finding citing its statute and showing its derivation step by step, and a citation-gated assistant that refuses when it cannot source). Procurement integrity (a detection grid computable from published fields: single-bid awards, short bid windows, threshold splitting, vendor concentration, repeat pairings, corrigendum churn, award-versus-estimate deviation, year-end clustering, shared-address bidders, set-aside shortfalls). Legislative and regulatory drafting (instruments modelled as obligations, thresholds, definitions, exemptions, commencement and repeal, so contradictions surface mechanically and are shown side by side without the system picking a winner). Disaster management and weather (gauges, reservoirs, wards and villages joined to officers, standing orders and escalation ladders, so a warning becomes an owned and dated task list and silence escalates on its own). Local bodies and constituency offices (nothing exists without an owner and a next date). Public sector oversight (a verified roster where every value opens its source document, unsourced values stay null and are reported as gaps, and overlap is shown as verbatim objects clauses side by side rather than asserted). Sequencing rule: start with registers the department already owns; anything needing another agency's cooperation comes last and is marked optional.
- **From Research to a Story Ready to Run** (https://thothica.com/use-cases/media/). Continuous coverage that stops at an editor; a research desk turning filings, reports, orders and transcripts into a brief with the angle and the supporting passages; analytics built on a real content taxonomy so coverage figures are facts rather than artefacts of loose tagging; and discourse measured at claim level rather than as a sentiment score, with every count opening the posts beneath it.
- **The Office Keeps Its Judgement. The Machine Keeps the Record.** (https://thothica.com/use-cases/legal/). Judgment and order translation where a controlled glossary of legal terms is binding input, the whole document is read and a strategy fixed before translation begins, passages are translated with that strategy and prior context so terminology cannot drift, and each passage is scored and retranslated rather than shipped with a caveat; output is a properly formatted legal document rather than a text file. Also structured case files (parties, issues, positions per issue, authorities per position, facts with their evidencing document, procedural history) and contradiction analysis across a body of law. Deployed per practice with its own glossary and store, invitation-only access, metered work, full audit log, and the option to run entirely on the firm's own infrastructure, because privileged material is never pooled.
- **Systems That Run Where Nothing May Leave the Building** (https://thothica.com/use-cases/defence/). Designed for disconnected operation: structuring, indexing and validation happen at build time so the running system needs no external call. Doctrine and standing orders modelled with amendment state, superseded material marked rather than deleted. Multi-source assessment keeping source reliability and information credibility as separate recorded properties that are never averaged together, with corroboration recorded only between genuinely independent sources. Also maintenance and readiness, logistics alias resolution, procurement qualification, lessons learned, and unit archives. Explicitly excluded: targeting systems, autonomous decisions in the use of force, and presenting machine output as an assessment.
- **Unstructured Material Turned Into Training-Grade Structure** (https://thothica.com/use-cases/ai-companies/). Domain corpora acquired with originals preserved byte-exact, read and typed with stable addresses, and delivered against a published schema with provenance and licence position on every record and documented gaps. The governing rule is that model output is never recorded as a fact: ground facts stay verbatim in their own field with source and locator, while anything normalised, classified or inferred is a derived value carrying method, confidence and what it came from. Also uncontaminated evaluation sets scored deterministically against exact passages, and grounded retrieval over structure rather than a vector database, delivered as operations any assistant can call.

## Open source: the method, in public

- Falsafa.ai (https://falsafa.ai), Thothica's open-source library of the world's philosophical, classical and religious texts. It holds more than 2,000 works, divided into more than 1.3 million passages that can each be quoted and cited exactly. On top of the library Thothica builds the Atlas, a map of the collection drawn from the texts themselves: it records the people, ideas, places, groups, events and objects that appear across twenty-five centuries of writing, and every time one text cites another it records how, whether the later author treated the earlier one as an authority, agreed with it, extended it, or argued against it. Every entry is tied to a paragraph that can be read in place. The software that builds the Atlas cannot write quotations; it only points at paragraphs, and the words are attached afterwards from the source text, so an invented quotation is impossible.

## One layer, rebuilt against every system

The same software does all of it. On one government portal it made 115,652 decisions about what the data meant. In a historical archive it read more than 1,000 works and recorded who was mentioned in each one, on what subject and in what context. For a publisher it has drafted hundreds of illustrated books on its own, researching each one first and citing a real source on every line.

Four unrelated industries: five government portals, a scanned archive in five languages, a library of more than 2,000 works spanning twenty-five centuries, and a publisher's research and production line. No two stored data the same way. The same layer was rebuilt against each, and the method did not change once. There is more running now that has not been announced.
